science.heading: SCIENCE INSTRUMENTS
science.sub: The Voyager twins originally carried 11 science instruments each. Status below reflects the latest official NASA information — not assumed.
power.heading: POWER SYSTEM
power.sub: Each spacecraft is powered by Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs), which convert heat from decaying plutonium-238 into electricity.
power.decline: Combined RTG output declines by about 4 watts per year, requiring the mission team to progressively power down instruments.

methodology.heading: DATA & METHODOLOGY
methodology.official.title: Official
methodology.official.body: Figures reported directly by NASA Science / JPL publications.
methodology.calculated.title: Calculated
methodology.calculated.body: Straightforward unit conversions or math performed on official NASA figures (e.g. km ↔ AU, light-time).
methodology.estimated.title: Estimated
methodology.estimated.body: Projected from the latest official NASA baseline position using the official escape velocity and elapsed time. Not live telemetry.
methodology.historical.title: Historical
methodology.historical.body: Fixed historical facts from NASA mission records (launch dates, flybys, interstellar crossing dates).
methodology.formula.title: Estimation formula
methodology.unavailable.title: When official data is unavailable
methodology.unavailable.body: The site shows "Official real-time data unavailable" and falls back to a calculated estimate — it never fabricates telemetry.
sources.heading: DATA SOURCES
sources.note: NASA is the primary and authoritative source for all mission data on this site. Wikipedia links are provided only as supplementary background reading.
sources.eyes: For an official real-time 3D visualization, see NASA Eyes on the Solar System. Our visualization is an educational companion to NASA’s official resources, not a replacement.
